features.name: Development Tool Shell
features.purpose: Establishes a consistent, minimal-chrome informational register (a status strip plus primary navigation) used across every screen, replacing a decorative marketing-style presentation with a compact developer-tool look.

invocation.trigger: The app loads, or any screen renders (the shell wraps every screen).

inputs.name: working_directory
inputs.description: The current project's working directory path.

inputs.name: round_identifier
inputs.description: The current round number.

inputs.name: default_provider_and_model
inputs.description: The currently selected default LLM provider and model.

inputs.name: app_version
inputs.description: The current app version identifier.

outputs.primary: A persistent status strip and primary navigation shown around every screen's content.
outputs.schema_notes: Status strip fields appear in fixed order (directory, round, provider/model, version); navigation entries appear in fixed order (Project, Artifacts, Settings, Docs).

success_criteria: The status strip always shows the current directory, round, provider/model, and version.
Navigation is present and identical across all screens.
No decorative elements (hero spacing, gradients, glow effects, emoji) appear anywhere.
Vertical spacing is visibly tighter than the prior presentation.
Only one accent emphasis color is used anywhere for primary emphasis or active-state indication.

failure_modes.mode: Status strip shows a stale directory or round after a change.
failure_modes.mitigation: Always recompute status strip fields from current session state on every render.

failure_modes.mode: Accent emphasis color leaks into secondary or decorative elements.
failure_modes.mitigation: Restrict accent color usage strictly to primary emphasis and active-state indication.

features.name: Open To The Project
features.purpose: Skips any introductory screen and takes the user straight into their project when a working directory is already known, so returning users land on their work immediately.

inputs.name: remembered_working_directory
inputs.description: A working directory remembered from a prior visit, if any.

outputs.primary: Navigation to either the project view or the directory picker.
outputs.schema_notes: Exactly one destination is chosen based on whether a working directory is remembered and still valid.

success_criteria: When a directory was remembered, opening root goes directly to the project view with no intermediate screen.
When no directory is remembered, the directory picker opens.
No introduction or landing screen ever appears.

failure_modes.mode: A remembered directory that no longer exists is opened anyway.
failure_modes.mitigation: Detect an invalid directory and fall back to the directory picker.

failure_modes.mode: Visible flicker between the picker and the project view on load.
failure_modes.mitigation: No landing layout is ever rendered; the page container stays empty until the routing callback resolves the destination.

features.name: Round Tree
features.purpose: Shows the current round's full set of expected artifacts as an ordered tree with per-artifact status, so the user can see at a glance what exists, what's outdated, and what's missing.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or the current round's artifacts change.

inputs.name: round_identifier
inputs.description: The current round number.

inputs.name: artifact_dependency_graph
inputs.description: The known upstream/downstream relationships between pipeline artifacts.

inputs.name: artifact_existence_and_timestamps
inputs.description: Which artifacts exist and when each was last produced.

outputs.primary: An ordered list of artifacts with status and lane coloring.
outputs.schema_notes: One entry per pipeline artifact, in pipeline order, each carrying a status (present, needs update, missing) and a lane (prompt for the agent, reference for the agent, record for you).

success_criteria: Every pipeline artifact for the round appears exactly once, in pipeline order.
An artifact whose upstream dependency is newer shows needs-update.
An artifact that does not exist shows missing.
The usage record never shows needs-update regardless of upstream changes.
A three-item legend explains the lane distinctions.
Only the current round's artifacts are shown.

failure_modes.mode: Status miscalculated when dependency information or timestamps are unavailable.
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat unknown state as missing rather than present.

failure_modes.mode: Usage record incorrectly flagged as needing update.
failure_modes.mitigation: Exempt the usage record explicitly from the needs-update calculation.

features.name: Agent Rows
features.purpose: Presents the seven pipeline agents as compact status rows, each showing what it produces, what it last ran on, its token usage this round, and the next available action, replacing a heavier presentation.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or an agent's run state changes.

inputs.name: agent_pipeline_order
inputs.description: The seven agents in fixed pipeline order.

inputs.name: agent_produced_artifact
inputs.description: The artifact each agent produces.

inputs.name: agent_last_run_model
inputs.description: The model each agent last ran on this round, from the round's usage totals.

inputs.name: agent_token_counts
inputs.description: Tokens in and out for each agent this round.

inputs.name: agent_action_state
inputs.description: The current action state for each agent (Start, Continue, Modify, Needs Update, Not Ready, Required).

outputs.primary: One row per agent showing name, produced artifact, last-run model, token counts, and action.
outputs.schema_notes: Rows appear in pipeline order; a blank model field indicates the agent has not run this round.

success_criteria: All seven agents appear in pipeline order every time.
An agent that has not run this round shows a blank model field, never a placeholder value.
Token counts reflect only the current round.
The action shown for each agent matches the existing state-routing rules.
No step numbers, prose descriptions, or emoji appear on any row.

Activating a row's action navigates to that agent exactly as the prior agent-select buttons did; an agent with an in-progress conversation and no artifact shows Continue and resumes that conversation.

failure_modes.mode: Stale action state shown after an artifact updates elsewhere.
failure_modes.mitigation: Recompute action state from current artifact and dependency status on every render.
Scope token aggregation strictly to the active round's usage record.

features.name: Round Cost
features.purpose: Surfaces the round's running estimated cost so the user always knows what they've spent before deciding whether to continue.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or the round's usage record changes.

inputs.name: round_usage_totals
inputs.description: Token totals and priced/unpriced call information for the current round.

outputs.primary: A labelled estimated-cost figure with supporting token counts.
outputs.schema_notes: Three lines: labelled estimate, token totals, and any calls excluded from pricing named individually.

success_criteria: The figure is always labelled as an estimate, never presented as exact.
Any call that could not be priced is named rather than silently dropped or shown as zero.
The total is never displayed as a zero-cost figure when some usage is unpriced.
The figure updates whenever the underlying usage record changes.

failure_modes.mode: Unpriced usage silently ignored, making the total look lower than reality.
failure_modes.mitigation: Always name excluded calls alongside the total.

failure_modes.mode: Cost shown as exactly zero when data is simply unavailable.
failure_modes.mitigation: Distinguish 'no usage yet' from 'usage present but unpriced'.

features.name: Artifact View
features.purpose: Lets the user open and read any artifact from any round without leaving the app, giving full visibility into what each agent produced or is expected to produce.

invocation.trigger: The user navigates to the Artifacts destination, or selects a file from a round tree or link elsewhere in the app.

inputs.name: round_identifier
inputs.description: The round to display, defaulting to the active round.

inputs.name: selected_file_path
inputs.description: The artifact selected for viewing within the chosen round.

inputs.name: rounds_on_disk
inputs.description: Every round present for the current project.

outputs.primary: The rendered content of the selected artifact, or a missing-file message.
outputs.format: Two-part screen: a round/tree selector and a content pane
outputs.schema_notes: The content pane shows a one-line header (path, size, last modified, lane) followed by the file's content — structured content pretty-printed, plain text shown with line numbers; a missing file shows 'missing — produced by {Agent}' in place of content.

success_criteria: Selecting any listed artifact displays its content correctly, with line numbers for every text file (JSON included, pretty-printed).
Only files that belong to the reviewed artifact set can ever be opened, and no path outside the project's spec folder can be reached this way.
Switching rounds updates both the tree and the available files.
The file that renders the app's mock output can also be opened in a rendered, viewable form separate from its raw text.
A way to obtain a copy of the currently viewed file is always available.
A missing artifact is shown in the tree and clearly explained when selected.

failure_modes.mode: A request for a file outside the recognized artifact set is attempted.
failure_modes.mitigation: Reject any path not present in the reviewed artifact table, resolved strictly within the project's spec folder.

failure_modes.mode: Viewing a very large file causes the screen to become unresponsive.
failure_modes.mitigation: Apply line numbering and rendering that scales to large plain-text files.

failure_modes.mode: Stale round list after a new round is created.
failure_modes.mitigation: Recompute the list of rounds on disk each time the screen opens.

features.name: Artifact Links
features.purpose: Makes every artifact reference in the app clickable, so the round tree and chat outputs consistently lead into the Artifact View instead of leaving the user to hunt for files.

invocation.trigger: The user selects a line in the round tree, or selects an open-artifact control in the chat frame's action row.

inputs.name: target_file_path
inputs.description: The artifact the user wants to open.

inputs.name: target_round
inputs.description: The round the artifact belongs to, defaulting to the current round.

outputs.primary: Navigation to the Artifact View with the requested file pre-selected.
outputs.schema_notes: The destination always resolves to the exact file/round pairing the user selected.

success_criteria: Every round-tree line opens the Artifact View at that exact file.
Every place a copy of a file can be obtained from the chat frame also offers a way to open it in place.
The Artifacts navigation entry is present in the app's primary navigation, positioned between Project and Settings.

failure_modes.mode: A link opens the wrong file or round after a round changes mid-session.
failure_modes.mitigation: Resolve the target at the moment of selection, not at render time.

failure_modes.mode: The navigation entry is missing from a screen that should offer it.
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the navigation register consistent across all screens.

features.name: Chat Frame Register
features.purpose: Restyles the existing chat/run interaction surface to match the developer-tool register — a plain-text pipeline indicator, block-style transcript, consistent cost reporting, and outline-style secondary actions — while preserving every existing function.

invocation.trigger: The user is on the chat frame for any agent's run.

inputs.name: agent_pipeline_state
inputs.description: The seven agents in order along with which is active, completed, or unreachable.

inputs.name: transcript_messages
inputs.description: The messages exchanged during the run.

inputs.name: live_progress_signal
inputs.description: Elapsed time and character counters reflecting live activity.

inputs.name: turn_token_counts
inputs.description: Token counts for the current turn.

inputs.name: run_cost_on_completion
inputs.description: The completed run's usage/cost summary.

inputs.name: retry_and_breadth_panel_state
inputs.description: State needed to show retry and breadth options.

outputs.primary: A rendered chat frame with restyled pipeline indicator, transcript, action row, composer, and progress signal.
outputs.schema_notes: Pipeline indicator lists all seven agents in order with active/completed/unreachable states; transcript is a sequence of speaker-labelled blocks; completed-run cost uses the same three-line summary as round cost.

success_criteria: All prior functions remain reachable and working: pipeline indicator, transcript, progress signal, turn tokens, fast-forward with its explanatory panel, retry, breadth, downloads, continue, composer, model indicator, status line.
The pipeline indicator shows plain text with no connecting arrows and correctly reflects active/completed/unreachable state.
No per-agent or pipeline-level back control remains, since equivalent navigation exists via the pipeline indicator and the status strip.
Transcript blocks show a dimmed one-word speaker label and no filled background.
The transcript's default height is noticeably taller than before while remaining independently scrollable.
On run completion, cost is shown in the same three-line form used elsewhere.
Exactly one strongly emphasized action exists per row (the continue action); all others are neutral outlines, except the rescan action shown in a warning tone.
The live-activity signal is the only moving element on the screen.
Chars, turn-token and elapsed counters, and the model name in the model chip, render in monospace.

failure_modes.mode: Removing back controls leaves a run state unreachable from the pipeline indicator.
failure_modes.mitigation: Verify every navigable state remains reachable via the pipeline indicator or status strip before removing legacy controls.

failure_modes.mode: Transcript height change breaks scroll behavior at small viewport sizes.
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the transcript independently scrollable regardless of viewport size.

failure_modes.mode: The completion cost strip fails to match the round-cost presentation.
failure_modes.mitigation: Source both from the same cost-estimation output.

nfr_goals: All artifact reads are strictly confined to the current project's spec folder, with no other path ever reachable.
Provider keys never leave the browser under any feature in this round.
Screens render fast enough to feel instantaneous for local file and round data (sub-second).
The visual and navigational register is fully consistent across every screen in the app.
Viewing or obtaining a copy of an artifact works consistently regardless of round or file size, without noticeable delay for typical spec file sizes.
